audio: Where is the nearest post office?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
choices: It's two blocks from here, on the left.
ex: Question en « Where » : on attend un lieu. Piège classique du TOEIC : « posted » reprend un mot proche de « post office ».

q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
ex: « When » = quand : on attend un moment.

audio: Who is in charge of the new project?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
ex: « Who is in charge of » = qui est responsable de : on attend une personne.

audio: Would you like me to print the report for you?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
choices: Yes, that would be great, thanks.
ex: C'est une proposition d'aide : on accepte ou on refuse poliment.

q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
ex: « Why » = pourquoi : on attend une cause. « For about two hours » répond à « How long ».

audio: How often do you visit the London office?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.

audio: Haven't you finished the presentation yet?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
choices: Almost, I just need to add the charts.
ex: Question négative : on répond sur l'état d'avancement. Les autres réponses reprennent juste le mot « presentation ».

audio: Should we take a taxi or walk to the restaurant?
q: Écoute la question, puis choisis la meilleure réponse.
ex: Question à choix (A or B) : on ne répond pas par « yes » ou « no », on choisit.

audio: Attention, passengers. The six fifteen train to Manchester will depart from platform four instead of platform two. We apologize for any inconvenience.
ex: « from platform four instead of platform two » : c'est le quai qui change.

audio: Hi Tom, it's Sarah from accounting. I'm calling about the invoice you sent on Monday. The total seems to be missing the delivery charge. Could you send me a corrected version by Thursday? Thanks.
q: What does Sarah ask Tom to do?
ex: « Could you send me a corrected version » : elle demande une facture corrigée.

audio: Welcome to the Greenfield Museum. The museum is open every day from nine a.m. to six p.m., except Mondays. Guided tours start every hour at the main entrance.
ex: « every day … except Mondays » = tous les jours sauf le lundi.

audio: Good morning everyone. Before we start, I'd like to remind you that the fire drill is scheduled for this afternoon at two o'clock. When the alarm rings, please leave the building by the nearest exit.
q: What will happen at two o'clock?

audio: Thank you for calling Bright Dental. Our office is currently closed. If you'd like to make an appointment, please press one. For emergencies, please call our partner clinic.
q: Why would a caller press one?
ex: « If you'd like to make an appointment, please press one ».

audio: Excuse me, is this seat taken? No, go ahead. Are you here for the marketing conference too? Yes, I'm giving a talk this afternoon about social media.
q: What will the woman who asked about the seat do this afternoon?
ex: « I'm giving a talk this afternoon » : présent continu pour un projet prévu.

audio: Due to road works on Main Street, the number twelve bus will not stop at City Hall this week. Passengers should use the stop on Park Avenue instead.
q: Where should passengers catch the bus this week?
ex: « should use the stop on Park Avenue instead » : à la place.

audio: Hello, this is a message for Mr. Garcia. Your order of office chairs has arrived at our store. You can pick it up any day this week between ten and five. Please bring your receipt.
ex: receipt = reçu, ticket de caisse. « pick it up » = venir le chercher.
